Blast.description: Rice Blast is one of the most destructive fungal diseases of rice caused by Magnaporthe oryzae. It affects leaves, stems, nodes, and panicles, reducing grain yield significantly under favorable environmental conditions.
symptoms: Diamond-shaped lesions with gray or white centers.
Neck blast causes panicle breakage and empty grains.
causes: Frequent rainfall or prolonged leaf wetness.
treatment: Spray Azoxystrobin if symptoms are severe.
prevention: Monitor crops regularly during humid weather.
Remove infected crop residues after harvest.

Brownspot.description: Brown Spot is a fungal disease caused by Bipolaris oryzae. It commonly occurs under nutrient-deficient conditions and may significantly reduce grain quality and yield.
symptoms: Small circular or oval brown lesions.
Lesions increase in size during severe infection.
treatment: Apply Propiconazole if disease spreads rapidly.
Improve soil fertility using balanced fertilizers.

Bacterialblight.description: Bacterial Blight is a serious bacterial disease caused by Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae. It spreads rapidly under rainy and windy conditions and can severely reduce rice productivity.
symptoms: Drying of entire leaves under severe infection.
causes: Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae bacterial infection.
treatment: Consult local agricultural guidelines for bacterial disease management.

Tungro.description: Rice Tungro Disease is a viral disease caused by Rice Tungro Bacilliform Virus (RTBV) and Rice Tungro Spherical Virus (RTSV). It is transmitted by green leafhoppers and is one of the most damaging viral diseases in rice.
treatment: No direct cure exists after viral infection.
prevention: Synchronize planting dates within the region.
Remove volunteer rice plants and weeds.
Regularly monitor fields for insect vectors.
